ada-boni.name: Ada Boni
ada-boni.summary: Italian chef and food writer (1881–1973) whose 1928 cookbook 'Il talismano della felicità' remains a classic of Italian cuisine.

il-cucchiaio-d-argento.name: Il cucchiaio d'argento
il-cucchiaio-d-argento.summary: A major Italian cookbook first published in 1950 by the magazine Domus, containing about 2,000 recipes from across Italy and reissued through eleven editions.

caciocavallo.name: Caciocavallo
caciocavallo.summary: A teardrop-shaped, stretched-curd cheese made from sheep's or cow's milk, produced across southern Italy.

manitoba-flour.name: Manitoba flour
manitoba-flour.summary: A strong wheat flour originating in the Canadian province of Manitoba, used chiefly in Italy and distinguished from weaker flours by measurements on a Chopin alveograph.

trastevere.name: Trastevere
trastevere.summary: A historic district (rione) of Rome, Italy, whose name means 'beyond the Tiber.'

alberto-grandi.name: Alberto Grandi
alberto-grandi.summary: Italian academic, born 1967, professor of Economics and Management at the University of Parma.

rationalism-architecture.name: Italian Rationalism
rationalism-architecture.summary: Architectural movement developed mainly in Italy during the 1920s and 1930s, based on the belief that design problems could be resolved through reason rather than historicism.

historicism-art.name: Historicism
historicism-art.summary: Artistic styles, especially in 19th-century architecture, that draw inspiration from recreating or imitating earlier historic styles.

benito-mussolini.name: Benito Mussolini
benito-mussolini.summary: Italian dictator (1883–1945) who founded fascism and led Italy from 1922 until his overthrow in 1943; executed by the Italian resistance in 1945.

eur-rome.name: EUR
eur-rome.summary: A residential and business district in Rome originally built for a 1942 World's Fair Mussolini planned to mark twenty years of Fascism, though the exhibition itself never took place.

michelangelo-antonioni.name: Michelangelo Antonioni
michelangelo-antonioni.summary: Italian film director (1912–2007) known for his 'alienation trilogy' and Blowup, whose visually striking, enigmatic films influenced world art cinema.

l-eclisse.name: L'Eclisse
l-eclisse.summary: A 1962 Italian romantic drama directed by Michelangelo Antonioni, starring Alain Delon and Monica Vitti, and the third film in his acclaimed trilogy; it won a Special Jury Prize at Cannes.

bernardo-bertolucci.name: Bernardo Bertolucci
bernardo-bertolucci.summary: An Italian film director (1941–2018) known for films like The Conformist and Last Tango in Paris, and the first Italian to win the Academy Award for Best Director, for The Last Emperor.

the-conformist-1970-film.name: The Conformist
the-conformist-1970-film.summary: A 1970 Italian political drama directed by Bernardo Bertolucci, based on Alberto Moravia's novel, about a Fascist functionary ordered to assassinate his former professor in 1930s Paris.

federico-fellini.name: Federico Fellini
federico-fellini.summary: An Italian film director and screenwriter (1920–1993), regarded as one of cinema's most influential filmmakers, known for films such as La Dolce Vita and 8½.

gruppo-7.name: Gruppo 7
gruppo-7.summary: A group of Italian architects founded in 1926 who promoted Rationalism, aiming for a middle ground between classicism and industrial-era architecture.

giuseppe-terragni.name: Giuseppe Terragni
giuseppe-terragni.summary: An Italian architect (1904–1943) who pioneered Rationalist modernism under Mussolini's regime, best known for the Casa del Fascio in Como, built 1932–1936.

palazzo-della-civilt-italiana.name: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana
palazzo-della-civilt-italiana.summary: A monumental 1938 building in Rome's EUR district, nicknamed the 'Square Colosseum,' built as an example of fascist architecture reflecting Mussolini's regime and inaugurated unfinished in 1940.

ernesto-lapadula.name: Ernesto Lapadula
ernesto-lapadula.summary: Italian architect and urban planner (1902–1968) who co-designed Rome's Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana with Giovanni Guerrini and Mario Romano.

metaphysical-painting.name: Metaphysical painting
metaphysical-painting.summary: An early 20th-century Italian art movement begun by Giorgio de Chirico in 1910, known for dreamlike scenes with sharp light and shadow and a mysterious, unsettling quality.

giacomo-balla.name: Giacomo Balla
giacomo-balla.summary: Italian painter and poet (1871 to 1958), a key figure in Futurism known for depicting light, movement and speed.

giorgio-morandi.name: Giorgio Morandi
giorgio-morandi.summary: Italian painter and printmaker (1890–1964) known for subtly muted still-life paintings of ceramic vessels, flowers and landscapes.

carlo-carr.name: Carlo Carrà
carlo-carr.summary: Italian painter (1881–1966) and a leading figure of the Futurist movement, who also wrote books on art and taught for many years in Milan.

giorgio-de-chirico.name: Giorgio de Chirico
giorgio-de-chirico.summary: Greek-Italian artist and writer (1888–1978) who founded the scuola metafisica movement before World War I, influencing the surrealists with dreamlike arcades and mannequins.

maxxi.name: MAXXI
maxxi.summary: National museum of contemporary art and architecture in Rome, designed by Zaha Hadid, which won the Stirling Prize in 2010.

giuseppe-pagano.name: Giuseppe Pagano
giuseppe-pagano.summary: An Italian architect and photographer (1896–1945) known for rationalist architecture up to the end of World War II, who was also a long-time editor of the magazine Casabella.

casabella.name: Casabella
casabella.summary: A monthly Italian magazine covering architecture and product design, known for interviews with prominent architects.

edoardo-persico.name: Edoardo Persico
edoardo-persico.summary: An Italian architecture and art critic, designer and essayist (1900-1936).

tendenza.name: Tendenza
tendenza.summary: An Italian neo-rationalist architecture movement of the 1960s-70s that reacted against modernism by emphasizing historical memory and traditional urban forms.

carlo-aymonino.name: Carlo Aymonino
carlo-aymonino.summary: Italian architect and urban planner (1926–2010) best known for the Monte Amiata housing complex in Milan.

aldo-rossi.name: Aldo Rossi
aldo-rossi.summary: Italian architect and designer (1931–1997), a leading figure of postmodernism and the first Italian to win the Pritzker Prize for architecture.

giorgio-grassi.name: Giorgio Grassi
giorgio-grassi.summary: Italian architect (born 1935) of the rationalist "La Tendenza" school with Aldo Rossi and Carlo Aymonino, known for severely simple, historically referenced designs.

milan-triennial.name: Milan Triennial
milan-triennial.summary: An art and design exhibition held every three years at the Triennale di Milano Museum in Italy.

reich-chancellery.name: New Reich Chancellery
reich-chancellery.summary: The new headquarters building for the German chancellor in Berlin, completed in early 1939 and seriously damaged and later demolished after World War II.

manfredo-tafuri.name: Manfredo Tafuri
manfredo-tafuri.summary: An Italian Marxist architectural historian and critic (1935–1994) noted for challenging the idea of the Renaissance as a 'golden age' and for critiquing earlier historians' 'operative criticism'.

universit-iuav-di-venezia.name: Iuav University of Venice
universit-iuav-di-venezia.summary: A university in Venice founded in 1926 as one of Italy's first architecture schools, now teaching architecture, urban planning, fashion, arts and design.

italian-campaign-world-war-ii.name: Italian Campaign
italian-campaign-world-war-ii.summary: Allied and Axis military operations in and around Italy from 1943 to 1945, beginning with the invasion of Sicily and ending with the Axis surrender in Italy in May 1945.

axis-powers.name: Rome-Berlin Axis
axis-powers.summary: The original 1936 alliance between Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, later joined by Japan to form the wider Axis powers of World War II.

pact-of-steel.name: Pact of Steel
pact-of-steel.summary: A 1939 military and political alliance between Germany and Italy, one of the agreements forming the basis of the Axis alliance.

victor-emmanuel-iii.name: Victor Emmanuel III
victor-emmanuel-iii.summary: King of Italy from 1900 until his abdication in 1946, who also briefly held the titles Emperor of Ethiopia and King of the Albanians; his reign spanned both World Wars and the Fascist era.

italian-resistance-movement.name: Italian resistance movement
italian-resistance-movement.summary: Coalition of Italian anti-fascist groups who fought Nazi German occupying forces and the collaborationist Italian Social Republic from 1943 to 1945, helping liberate Italy.

italian-social-republic.name: Italian Social Republic
italian-social-republic.summary: A German puppet state led by Mussolini in northern and central Italy from 1943 to 1945, popularly known as the Republic of Salò, dependent on German troops to maintain control.

pope-pius-xii.name: Pope Pius XII
pope-pius-xii.summary: Head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 1939 to 1958, whose conduct during the Holocaust remains debated between accusations of silence and claims of quiet aid to Jews.

franklin-d-roosevelt.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
franklin-d-roosevelt.summary: 32nd U.S. president (1933–1945) and the longest-serving in American history, who led the country through the Great Depression and World War II.

open-city.name: Open city
open-city.summary: Wartime designation for a settlement that renounces defense to avoid destruction, after which international law expects occupying forces to enter peacefully rather than attack.

francis-spellman.name: Francis Spellman
francis-spellman.summary: American Catholic prelate (1889–1967) who served as Archbishop of New York from 1939 and was made a cardinal by Pope Pius XII in 1946.

italian-co-belligerent-army.name: Italian Co-Belligerent Army
italian-co-belligerent-army.summary: Former Royal Italian Army units that fought alongside the Allies after Italy's September 1943 armistice, fielding roughly 266,000 to 326,000 troops in the Italian Campaign.

army-group-c.name: Army Group C
army-group-c.summary: German Wehrmacht army group of World War II, first defending the Franco-German border and later coordinating German forces on the Italian front until its surrender in 1945.

german-instrument-of-surrender.name: German Instrument of Surrender
german-instrument-of-surrender.summary: The document ending World War II in Europe, signed on 8 May 1945 in Berlin after an earlier surrender at Reims was rejected by the Soviet Union.

grazia-deledda.name: Grazia Deledda
grazia-deledda.summary: An Italian writer, 1871 to 1936, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1926 for her depictions of life on her native Sardinia, the first Italian woman to receive the prize.

luigi-pirandello.name: Luigi Pirandello
luigi-pirandello.summary: Italian dramatist, novelist and poet (1867–1936) awarded the 1934 Nobel Prize in Literature, whose tragic farces are seen as forerunners of the Theatre of the Absurd.

salvatore-quasimodo.name: Salvatore Quasimodo
salvatore-quasimodo.summary: An Italian poet and translator (1901-1968) who won the 1959 Nobel Prize in Literature and ranked among the foremost Italian poets of the 20th century.

eugenio-montale.name: Eugenio Montale
eugenio-montale.summary: An Italian poet, prose writer, editor and translator (1896–1981) awarded the 1975 Nobel Prize in Literature for his distinctive poetry.

dario-fo.name: Dario Fo
dario-fo.summary: Italian playwright, actor and political campaigner (1926–2016) who won the 1997 Nobel Prize in Literature, known for satirical theatre criticizing corruption and political leaders.

giovanni-pascoli.name: Giovanni Pascoli
giovanni-pascoli.summary: Italian poet and classical scholar (1855–1912), an emblematic decadent poet alongside Gabriele D'Annunzio, known for his intimate, childlike poetic sentiment.

italo-svevo.name: Italo Svevo
italo-svevo.summary: Pen name of Aron Hector Schmitz (1861–1928), an Italian and Austro-Hungarian writer and businessman, a close friend of James Joyce and a pioneer of the psychological novel.

gabriele-d-annunzio.name: Gabriele D'Annunzio
gabriele-d-annunzio.summary: Italian poet, playwright and army officer (1863–1938) who became a national war hero during World War I after a prominent literary and political career.

umberto-saba.name: Umberto Saba
umberto-saba.summary: Italian poet and novelist (1883 to 1957), born in Trieste, who later ran an antiquarian bookshop and suffered from depression throughout his adult life.

giuseppe-ungaretti.name: Giuseppe Ungaretti
giuseppe-ungaretti.summary: An Italian modernist poet (1888–1970) who debuted while fighting in World War I trenches and later led the experimental 'Hermeticism' movement in Italian poetry.

giuseppe-tomasi-di-lampedusa.name: Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa
giuseppe-tomasi-di-lampedusa.summary: A reserved Sicilian aristocrat and writer (1896–1957), of the last generation of Tomasi Princes of Lampedusa, remembered for his only novel, Il Gattopardo, published after his death in 1958.

umberto-eco.name: Umberto Eco
umberto-eco.summary: Italian medievalist, philosopher and novelist (1932 to 2016), best known for his 1980 novel The Name of the Rose, blending semiotics, biblical analysis and medieval studies.

the-name-of-the-rose.name: The Name of the Rose
the-name-of-the-rose.summary: Umberto Eco's 1980 debut novel, a historical murder mystery set in an Italian monastery in 1327, one of the best-selling books ever published.

six-characters-in-search-of-an-author.name: Six Characters in Search of an Author
six-characters-in-search-of-an-author.summary: An absurdist Italian play by Luigi Pirandello, first performed in 1921, exploring the relationship between authors, their characters and theatre.
six-characters-in-search-of-an-author.source_title: Six Characters in Search of an Author

zeno-s-conscience.name: Zeno's Conscience
zeno-s-conscience.summary: A 1923 novel by Italian writer Italo Svevo, presented as the fictional Zeno Cosini's memoirs for his psychoanalyst; praised by James Joyce and credited with Svevo's literary success.

leonardo-sciascia.name: Leonardo Sciascia
leonardo-sciascia.summary: An Italian writer, essayist, playwright and politician (1921–1989) whose novels, including Il giorno della civetta (The Day of the Owl), were adapted into several films.

the-day-of-the-owl.name: Il giorno della civetta
the-day-of-the-owl.summary: Crime novel about the Sicilian Mafia by Leonardo Sciascia, finished in 1960; the first fictional work for a mainstream readership to openly call the Mafia a criminal organization.

alberto-moravia.name: Alberto Moravia
alberto-moravia.summary: Italian novelist and journalist (1907–1990) whose works explored modern sexuality, alienation and existentialism, including The Conformist.

pier-paolo-pasolini.name: Pier Paolo Pasolini
pier-paolo-pasolini.summary: An Italian poet, writer and film director (1922 to 1975), a major and controversial figure in 20th-century Italian culture known for films like The Gospel According to St. Matthew and Salò, who was murdered in 1975.

house-of-savoy.name: House of Savoy
house-of-savoy.summary: A royal dynasty established in 1003 that expanded from the Alpine County of Savoy to rule Sicily, Sardinia and eventually the unified Kingdom of Italy until 1946.

armando-diaz.name: Armando Diaz
armando-diaz.summary: Italian general and Marshal of Italy (1861–1928) who led the Italian army as Chief of Staff from 1917 to a decisive victory at Vittorio Veneto, ending World War I on the Italian Front.

paolo-thaon-di-revel.name: Paolo Thaon di Revel
paolo-thaon-di-revel.summary: Italian admiral of the Regia Marina during World War I and later a politician, who lived from 1859 to 1948 and was given the honorary title Duke of the Sea.

luigi-rizzo.name: Luigi Rizzo
luigi-rizzo.summary: Italian admiral (1887–1951) nicknamed 'the Sinker' for sinking two Austro-Hungarian battleships as a torpedo boat commander in World War I.

guglielmo-marconi.name: Guglielmo Marconi
guglielmo-marconi.summary: An Italian engineer (1874–1937) credited as the inventor of radio for his wireless telegraph system, sharing the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics with Ferdinand Braun.

costanzo-ciano.name: Costanzo Ciano
costanzo-ciano.summary: Italian naval officer and politician (1876-1939), father of the former Italian foreign minister Galeazzo Ciano.

dino-grandi.name: Dino Grandi
dino-grandi.summary: Italian Fascist politician and ambassador (1895–1988) who was ennobled by Mussolini's government as Conte di Mordano.

cesare-maria-de-vecchi.name: Cesare Maria De Vecchi
cesare-maria-de-vecchi.summary: An Italian soldier, colonial administrator and fascist politician (1884-1959).

ettore-tolomei.name: Ettore Tolomei
ettore-tolomei.summary: An Italian nationalist and fascist (1865–1952) who became a member of the Italian Senate in 1923 and was ennobled as Conte della Vetta in 1937.

francesco-pacelli.name: Francesco Pacelli
francesco-pacelli.summary: Italian lawyer and canon-law expert (1872–1935), elder brother of Pope Pius XII, who as legal adviser to Pius XI helped negotiate the 1929 Lateran Treaty with Mussolini that established Vatican City.

world-congress-of-philosophy.name: World Congress of Philosophy
world-congress-of-philosophy.summary: A global gathering of philosophers held every five years since 1900 under the International Federation of Philosophical Societies, called this only from 1973 onward.

international-federation-of-philosophica.name: International Federation of Philosophical Societies
international-federation-of-philosophica.summary: The world organization for national philosophy societies, which sponsors the International Philosophy Olympiad and the World Congress of Philosophy held every five years.

stadio-olimpico.name: Stadio Olimpico
stadio-olimpico.summary: Rome's largest sports venue, built from 1928 and opened in 1953, home to football clubs S.S. Lazio and A.S. Roma.

scuderia-ferrari.name: Scuderia Ferrari
scuderia-ferrari.summary: Ferrari's racing division and Formula One team, founded by Enzo Ferrari in 1929; the oldest surviving F1 team, holding a record 16 Constructors' Championships.

global-language-monitor.name: Global Language Monitor
global-language-monitor.summary: A company based in Austin, Texas, that analyzes trends in the English language.

italian-national-institute-of-statistics.name: ISTAT
italian-national-institute-of-statistics.summary: Italy's national statistics institute, the country's main source of official data including its census and major economic and social surveys.

as-roma.name: A.S. Roma
as-roma.summary: A professional football club in Rome founded in 1927, one of Italy's most successful clubs, which shares the Stadio Olimpico with city rival Lazio.

ss-lazio.name: S.S. Lazio
ss-lazio.summary: An Italian professional sports club based in Rome, founded in 1900, best known for its football team and its rivalry with fellow Rome club Roma.

francesco-totti.name: Francesco Totti
francesco-totti.summary: Italian former professional footballer, born 1976, who spent his entire career at Roma, becoming its all-time top scorer and most capped player, and won the 2006 World Cup with Italy.

daniele-de-rossi.name: Daniele De Rossi
daniele-de-rossi.summary: Italian football manager and former midfielder (born 1983) who spent 18 seasons with Roma and won the 2006 World Cup with Italy.

bulgari.name: Bulgari
bulgari.summary: Italian luxury fashion house founded in Rome in 1884 by Sotirios Voulgaris, known for jewellery and watches and acquired by LVMH in 2011.

fendi.name: Fendi
fendi.summary: Italian luxury fashion house founded in Rome in 1925, known for fur and leather goods, which became part of the LVMH group in 2001.

valentino-fashion-house.name: Valentino
valentino-fashion-house.summary: An Italian luxury fashion house founded in 1960 by Valentino Garavani, with its creative direction based in Rome.

laura-biagiotti.name: Laura Biagiotti
laura-biagiotti.summary: Italian fashion designer, 1943 to 2017, who founded the House of Biagiotti.

italian-grand-prix.name: Italian Grand Prix
italian-grand-prix.summary: A motor race held since 1921, one of only two Grands Prix run every season since the Formula One World Championship began in 1950, almost always held at Monza.

monza-circuit.name: Monza Circuit
monza-circuit.summary: A race track near Milan built in 1922, the world's fourth purpose-built motor racing circuit and the oldest in mainland Europe, nicknamed 'the Temple of Speed.'

rome-film-festival.name: Rome Film Festival
rome-film-festival.summary: An annual film festival held in Rome each October, officially recognized as a competitive festival by the International Federation of Film Producers Associations in 2022.

franco-pinna.name: Franco Pinna
franco-pinna.summary: Italian photographer (1925–1978), one of the leading figures of neorealism, who worked in black and white.

juliet-of-the-spirits.name: Juliet of the Spirits
juliet-of-the-spirits.summary: A 1965 Federico Fellini fantasy film starring Giulietta Masina about a woman's visions and mysticism as she finds the strength to leave her unfaithful husband; it won a Golden Globe.
